title: JURI-AI: AI-Powered Legal Assistant Platform
summary: Enterprise-grade legal intelligence ecosystem featuring Google Gemini AI & Pinecone vector search for statutory advice, automated contract risk assessment, legal template Gallery, and verified lawyer consultation.
problem: Navigating statutory law and reviewing legal documents is costly, complex, and inaccessible to everyday citizens and small businesses.
dataset: Comprehensive Indian Statutory & Case Law Corpus (Constitution of India, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act, FEMA 1999, Consumer Protection Act 2019, Rent Control Act) vectorized with HuggingFace embeddings in Pinecone.
methodology: Triple-tier microservices: React/TypeScript frontend, Express.js API gateway with JWT RBAC, and FastAPI Python AI engine. RAG pipeline combines Pinecone top-k vector search with Google Gemini LLM for context-aware statutory answers and automated contract clause risk analysis.
keyResults: Sub-2s response latency, 95%+ query accuracy with statutory act citations, automated risk grading of 11+ contract clauses, and dynamic autofill for 20+ legal document templates.
role: AI Developer: Built FastAPI LangChain RAG pipeline, integrated Gemini AI with Pinecone vector store and deployed microservices on Railway.
challengesLearnings: Eliminated hallucinations in statutory queries through strict top-k Pinecone grounding. Managed asynchronous PDF document parsing in FastAPI without bottlenecking the Express gateway.
limitations: Provides informative legal intelligence and risk assessment; does not replace formal legal representation by a licensed attorney.

title: FinPulse: AI Financial & Earnings Call Research Copilot
summary: Institutional-grade RAG copilot analyzing corporate earnings call transcripts and SEC filings with numerical grounding, verifiable citations, and cross-company guidance inconsistency detection.
problem: Analyzing lengthy corporate earnings calls, SEC 10-K/10-Q filings, and financial metrics is slow and manual, while general LLMs hallucinate financial numbers and lack verifiable grounding.
dataset: Indexed earnings call transcripts and SEC reports across global enterprise technology leaders (NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet/Google, Tesla) with dynamic PDF/TXT/MD ingestion.
methodology: Dual-stage RAG architecture combining ChromaDB vector similarity search, BGE cross-encoder reranking, and citation synthesis with strict zero-hallucination guardrails and confidence scoring via Groq LLM inference.
keyResults: Instant financial Q&A with document-level citations and verbatim snippets, colored confidence badges (High/Medium/Low), and automated peer comparison reasoning (e.g., NVIDIA vs Microsoft CapEx).
role: Sole AI Developer: Engineered retrieval and cross-encoder reranking pipeline, implemented citation synthesis and confidence scoring, built Streamlit workspace UI, and deployed to Streamlit Community Cloud.
challengesLearnings: Eliminated financial hallucination by enforcing strict numerical grounding and BGE reranking over high-density chunks before synthesizing answers with source citations.
limitations: Context retrieval relies on indexed filings; real-time market trading feeds require separate live API streaming integrations.

title: StrengthCast: Concrete Compressive Strength Predictor
summary: Predicts concrete compressive strength from mix ratios and curing age using high-performance regression pipelines.
problem: Predict concrete compressive strength based on constituent mix proportions and curing duration, replacing slow 28-day physical cylinder break tests.
dataset: Concrete Compressive Strength dataset (cement, blast furnace slag, fly ash, water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, age in days).
methodology: Exploratory data analysis, scikit-learn ColumnTransformer preprocessing pipeline saved with joblib, and extensive regression model benchmarking.
keyResults: Compared Linear Regression (R² 0.63), Random Forest (R² 0.88), and XGBoost (R² 0.93, RMSE 4.28 MPa, MAE 2.96 MPa).
role: Sole ML Developer: Designed preprocessing pipeline, performed cross-validation & hyperparameter tuning, built and deployed interactive Streamlit web application.
challengesLearnings: Strength depends nonlinearly on curing age, which linear models miss completely. Successfully captured nonlinear interaction dynamics using tree ensemble pipelines.
limitations: Model predictions are calibrated specifically within the domain bounds of standard concrete constituent ratios and standard curing conditions.

title: Crop Recommendation System
summary: Recommends optimal crops across 22 categories using soil nutrients and meteorological parameters.
problem: Guide farmers in selecting the most viable crop to maximize yield based on localized soil chemistry and atmospheric conditions.
dataset: 22-class agricultural crop dataset containing N, P, K soil ratios, temperature, humidity, pH, and rainfall.
methodology: Multi-class classification pipeline comparing SVC, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest evaluated with GridSearchCV hyperparameter tuning, followed by confusion matrix error analysis.
keyResults: Random Forest achieved the best performance with ~99% test accuracy across 22 crop classes.
role: Sole ML Developer: Implemented multiclass classification modeling, automated grid search validation, and built web deployment interface.
challengesLearnings: In-depth error analysis revealed confusion primarily between rice and jute due to overlapping high-humidity and water requirement profiles.
limitations: Does not account for dynamic real-time market pricing or seasonal pests.

title: Diabetes Risk Prediction
summary: Predicts diagnostic diabetes onset probability using clinical patient physiological metrics.
problem: Provide early predictive risk assessment for diabetes onset to assist clinical screening workflows.
dataset: Clinical diabetes diagnostic dataset with patient blood glucose, BMI, insulin, age, and blood pressure markers.
methodology: Data preprocessing, feature scaling, classification benchmarking, and interactive deployment.
keyResults: Trained classification algorithms with validated ROC-AUC metrics and real-time inference.
role: ML Developer: Developed preprocessing, feature normalization pipeline, and interactive screening app.
challengesLearnings: Handled zero-value imputations for biological variables such as insulin and skinfold thickness.
limitations: Intended for screening assistance; clinical validation required.

title: Bank Marketing Campaign Predictor
summary: Predicts customer term-deposit subscriptions on 41k records addressing high class imbalance and data leakage.
problem: Optimize telemarketing targeting efficiency by predicting customer willingness to subscribe to long-term bank deposits while preventing target data leakage.
dataset: Bank Marketing dataset containing 41,000+ campaign records with high class imbalance (11% positive subscribers).
methodology: Removed the leaky 'duration' feature to ensure real-world predictive validity, handled 'unknown' categorical values cleanly inside the pipeline, applied class weights to balance 11% minority positives, and benchmarked a Keras Tuner-optimized ANN against XGBoost.
keyResults: Tuned ANN (ROC-AUC 0.799) vs XGBoost (ROC-AUC 0.811), both achieving ~65% recall on subscribers, delivering a 3.4x lift over random calling.
role: Sole ML/DL Researcher: Led exploratory data analysis, leakage auditing, pipeline design, hyperparameter search with Keras Tuner, and lift curve evaluation.
challengesLearnings: Identified that gradient boosting matched a tuned ANN with far less computational overhead and faster training iterations, highlighting the practical efficiency of tree ensembles for structured tabular data.
limitations: Phone campaign response dynamics can drift over varying macroeconomic interest rate cycles.

title: Employee Attrition Prediction
summary: Identifies organizational turnover drivers and leaver probabilities under severe class imbalance.
problem: Predict employee flight risk to enable proactive retention interventions in human resources management.
dataset: HR Employee Attrition dataset characterized by 16% positive leavers (84% retention).
methodology: Cross-validated classification models addressing imbalance; tested Logistic Regression with balanced weighting against an unweighted ANN to study class penalty effects.
keyResults: Logistic Regression won on cross-validated ROC-AUC (0.83) with recall 0.66 on leavers; untuned-for-imbalance ANN scored recall 0.32. [Add final ANN result after class weights.]
role: Sole Developer & Analyst: Investigated class imbalance techniques, designed evaluation matrices, and analyzed metric divergence between weighted linear models and neural networks.
challengesLearnings: Unequivocally demonstrated that deep neural networks require explicit class weighting or focal loss on tabular imbalanced sets; otherwise, gradients get overwhelmed by majority classes.
limitations: HR perception factors such as team morale and peer management dynamics are unquantified in static tabular records.

title: California Housing Price Prediction
summary: Deep neural network regression for housing median values with strict data-leakage safeguards.
problem: Estimate median California district housing values from demographic and geographical attributes.
dataset: California Housing dataset comprising 20,640 census block records.
methodology: ANN regression architecture using He normal weight initialization, batch normalization/dropout, early stopping, and outlier removal performed strictly on training splits only.
keyResults: Test R² of approximately 0.77 to 0.80 (RMSE ~0.51 to 0.55 in $100k units). [Add Linear/XGBoost baseline results if run.]
role: Sole DL Developer: Formulated regression architecture, engineered training/validation split protocols to prevent leakage, and resolved convergence anomalies.
challengesLearnings: Diagnosed and resolved a subtle training bug where features and targets were misaligned; detected it because loss plateaued suspiciously at the exact variance of the target variable.
limitations: Historical pricing census data does not reflect contemporary inflation and current real estate valuation shifts.

title: Stellar Object Classification
summary: Classifies SDSS astronomical objects into galaxies, quasars, and stars with spectral band ablation.
problem: Automate spectroscopic astronomical taxonomy for massive sky survey datasets from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS).
dataset: 25k SDSS spectral and photometric observation records across 3 classes: Galaxy, Quasar, and Star.
methodology: Trained and benchmarked ANN architectures and XGBoost under two experimental regimes: full spectrum with redshift versus photometric color bands only.
keyResults: With redshift: ANN achieved ~97% and XGBoost ~98% accuracy. Without redshift (photometric bands only): XGBoost 86% and ANN 75%, with stars being hardest to identify.
role: Sole ML/DL Researcher: Devised feature ablation experiments, trained classification models, and interpreted feature importance.
challengesLearnings: Discovered that a single feature (redshift) carried the vast majority of predictive discrimination; ablation proved the critical reliance models develop on dominant physical markers.
limitations: High sensitivity to redshift accuracy; photometric-only estimation struggles when spectral resolution is degraded.

title: Vehicle Type Classification
summary: Transfer learning computer vision model classifying 10 vehicle categories using MobileNetV2.
problem: Classify complex multi-class road transport vehicles across 10 diverse categories in real-world driving environments.
dataset: Multi-class vehicle imagery covering 10 distinct classes: bus, bike, CNG, easy-bike, hatchback, MPV, pickup, SUV, sedan, truck.
methodology: Transfer learning architecture utilizing MobileNetV2 backbone, in-model data augmentation layers (RandomFlip, RandomRotation, RandomZoom), followed by two-stage fine-tuning.
keyResults: Validation accuracy reached 85.9%; evaluated on a separate 100-image out-of-distribution test set yielding 71% accuracy. Weakest classes: pickup (confused with truck) and hatchback/sedan.
role: Computer Vision Developer: Architected transfer learning pipeline, built data pipelines with tf.data, implemented data augmentation, and debugged evaluation metrics.
challengesLearnings: Uncovered a label-order mismatch between folder directory alphanumeric sorting and training label indexing that caused the initial test score to show 42%; rectified the class mapping pipeline to unlock the true 71% generalization score.
limitations: Suffers from visual confusion in ambiguous angles between geometrically similar body shapes (pickup vs truck, sedan vs hatchback).

title: Age and Gender Estimation from Faces
summary: Multi-output CNN utilizing VGG16 with functional API for simultaneous age regression and gender classification.
problem: Simultaneously estimate human age (continuous regression) and binary gender (classification) from facial crops within a unified deep network.
dataset: UTKFace dataset containing 20k+ face images. Identified and excised ~43k duplicate files across redundant directory uploads prior to dataset splitting.
methodology: Multi-task learning architecture with shared VGG16 convolutional feature extractor branching into dual heads via Keras Functional API: linear activation for age regression (MSE/MAE loss) and sigmoid activation for gender (Binary Cross-Entropy).
keyResults: [Add test age MAE (baseline about 15 years for predicting the mean), gender accuracy, MAE by age group].
role: Computer Vision Researcher: Conducted dataset deduplication, implemented dual-output Keras functional graph, weighted multi-task loss functions, and conducted error audits.
challengesLearnings: Detected and removed ~43,000 duplicate images across multi-folder archives before training to prevent severe data leakage between train/val/test splits.
limitations: Dataset contains sparse representations for subjects aged >70, lacks longitudinal person IDs, and carries known demographic and illumination biases. Not deployed yet.
